profile.reading: This building is the second of two structures making up SFO4, part of Csquare Silicon Valley campus cluster at 1500 and 1550 Space Park Drive in Santa Clara, California, mapped as a separate OpenStreetMap way from its immediate neighbor. Csquare, Inc., trading on the New York Stock Exchange as CSQR, is the current name of a data center real estate company whose Silicon Valley facilities trace back to CenturyLink Savvis-heritage colocation assets, divested and rebranded Evoque Data Center Solutions around 2020 to 2021 under Brookfield-affiliated ownership, later Centersquare, and now Csquare ahead of its July 16, 2026 initial public offering. That IPO priced at 21 dollars per share across 50 million shares for roughly 1.05 billion dollars gross, and Brookfield Corporation retained approximately 69 percent of voting power afterward, making Csquare a controlled company under NYSE rules. Per Csquare own SEC registration prospectus, the company overall portfolio as of March 31, 2026 spanned 64 sites across 21 major metro markets in the US, Canada, and the UK, totaling roughly 389 megawatts of sellable power capacity and more than 1,700 customers, with CEO Spencer Mullee and CFO Steven Cook both having joined from the company Evoque-era leadership. That prospectus Properties table lists two Silicon Valley buildings under the SFO4 code, designated SFO4_A at 21,724 rentable square feet, leased, 86.8 percent occupied, and SFO4_B at 35,754 rentable square feet, company-owned and fully occupied at 100 percent, though which specific street address corresponds to which suffix could not be confirmed this session, so no single building-level square footage figure is assigned to this record individually. No tenant is named for either SFO4 unit in any source reviewed. The SFO airport-code naming convention applied here, despite the buildings sitting roughly 40 miles south of San Francisco International Airport itself, is common in the Bay Area colocation market, where operators historically used the nearest major airport code as market shorthand even for Santa Clara, Sunnyvale, and San Jose facilities rather than adopting the closer SJC code.

reading.body:
Csquare SFO4 in Santa Clara publishes 129.4 MW of combined utility power across 273,000 square feet of technical space, but does not separate IT load from total facility draw, leaving usable compute capacity unstated.

The facility holds six certifications spanning financial controls, information security, payment systems, federal compliance, and sustainable building standards. These qualify the campus to host regulated workloads, though which tenants invoke which certifications remains unpublished. The certifications themselves tell nothing about current occupancy, utilization, or whether the facility is built out or still under construction.

California has 103 data center facilities in this registry, yet only seven publish megawatt figures. SFO4's 129.4 MW exceeds the published capacity of every other facility in the state for which a number exists. This ranking is an artifact of extreme scarcity in disclosed capacity data. It does not indicate whether SFO4 is truly the largest facility in California by power, only that most operators do not publish this figure at all. The real constraint on AI scaling in the region remains invisible in public data.
